parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A clay WOMAN (an adult woman, not the man in the reference: copy only the reference's clay style, pose and framing) with an oversized bobble head, a thin neck and narrow straight shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Her whole figure is a translucent glowing RED hologram sculpted from see-through red resin-like clay, lit from within, thin horizontal scan lines across her and small glitching pixel offsets at her edges as if the projection flickers, a sharp short chin-length bob of glowing red light, perfectly straight, edges breaking into tiny pixels, square pixel-block tears of red light running down her cheeks like corrupted data. No mask: the face of a grown woman in her thirties, calm, expressionless and cold, with glowing white eyes with no pupils, a faint thin smile, perfectly smooth hologram skin. Wearing a simple sleek high-collared shift dress made of red light, flickering with scan lines, she holds no weapon: both hologram hands are raised with fingers spread, projecting a glowing lattice of thin bright red laser beams that criss-cross the air in front of her in a neat grid. A vast dark digital data centre that is also a prison of trapped souls: endless aisles of tall black server racks blinking with red lights and glowing red circuit grids running along the floor and walls, pale ghostly souls trapped inside glowing red wireframe data cages and pressed against the glass of the server screens, faint ghostly faces and hands pressed to the glass, thin streams of red light (no readable characters), sculpted as a miniature claymation diorama, softly out of focus behind her, no logos, no lettering. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, her body is in three-quarter view and her head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are raised and fully visible, fingers spread, projecting the red laser grid; nothing held in her hands. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora

The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a lopsided skull that sags and melts down one side, one cheek drooping lower than the other, pink flesh-toned clay skin, a greasy black comb-over, raised grey clay wrinkle ridges on the forehead. His huge oversized bobble head is entirely covered by a filthy lumpy burlap sack pulled all the way down over the whole skull and face, ragged cut eye holes, a cross-stitched mouth, rope tied tight at the neck; no skin or hair visible. The sack is pulled fully DOWN over the face with its eye holes right over his eyes, never pushed up on top of the head like a cap and never covering only half the face; on a pointed cone skull the sack covers the whole cone too. Wearing blood-soaked green surgeon's scrubs with a surgical cap and a stained surgical mask hanging round his neck, two heavy rusty pitted iron chains around his neck, one short and one hanging lower over his chest, his right fist grips a crude spear: a long wooden pole with a rusty jagged blade lashed to the top with wire and rag, held upright with the blade above his shoulder; his LEFT fist tightly grips a rusty pitchfork by its long wooden handle, held upright at his side with the rusty tines rising above his shoulder beside his head, carried in his hand, not strapped to his back. A rusty orange pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are full and both are tight clenched fists, knuckles toward the camera: the right fist grips the held weapon, the left fist grips the second weapon by its handle as described. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
